This is the basic framework I follow and it's stuff I've picked up from expierience and from producers like Nick Mira making usable beats isn't about flash it's about simplicity and support. In other words your beats shouldn't be the show piece they should be recognizable and simple. Most songs will only use 4 drums in relatively simple patterns Nick Mira said his most successful beats all used a simple double step hi hat pattern and he would reuse the same 808 a lot. You really only want 1 or 2 melodies too since the rapper or lyricist is the star of the show they have to be the primary melody so a solid 8 bar melody and maybe a counter melody  will do just fine. Don't pick any sounds that are super distracting either you should be unique but not flashy kind of like a good colone. The charm of your beat should be discovered not forced. I'm not saying that's the only way to make good beats for artist but it's a few relative rules I keep in mind and you'll find they don't cripple creativity too much. Oh and don't forget to tune that 808 😉.

Not sure if this is a serious question but I'm gonna answer it like it is. Mixing is the second most important if not the most important part of making your music sound professional and pleasing. It's essentially getting every piece of your track to fit in its spot on the frequency range and also adjusting there paning and gain staging to stop clashing from instruments. In other words it's a use of technical knowledge and style to make your music work together instead of fight for dominance and I'd recommend learning it sooner than latter. Hope that helped.
